articles.summary: BWH Hotels has notified guests that their reservation data was exposed in a recent cybersecurity incident. Customers are being advised to remain vigilant against potential phishing attempts resulting from the data breach.

articles.summary: A 15-year-old individual has been detained by French authorities for allegedly selling data stolen during a cyberattack against France Titres, the government agency responsible for administrative documents.

articles.title: Hackers Use Jenkins Access to Deploy DDoS Botnet Against Gaming Servers
articles.summary: Hackers are exploiting misconfigured Jenkins servers to deploy DDoS botnets specifically targeting gaming infrastructure, including systems owned by Valve Corporation.

articles.title: US government, allies publish guidance on how to safely deploy AI agents
articles.summary: The US government and international allies have issued new security guidelines addressing the risks associated with AI agents operating within critical infrastructure. The guidance highlights that many organizations are providing these agents with excessive network access that exceeds their current ability to monitor or control.

articles.title: Senate Judiciary advances bill that would bar minors from interacting with AI companions
articles.summary: The Senate Judiciary Committee has advanced the GUARD Act, which restricts minors' interactions with AI companions and mandates that AI disclose its non-human nature. The bill also criminalizes the solicitation or creation of sexual content involving minors by AI systems.

articles.title: Story retracted
articles.summary: BleepingComputer retracted a report regarding a data breach at Instructure after confirming the information was based on an outdated incident. No new breach has been verified.

articles.title: Federal agencies must patch cPanel bug by Sunday, CISA says
articles.summary: CISA has mandated that federal agencies patch a critical cPanel vulnerability, CVE-2026-41940, by this Sunday to prevent full system compromise. The flaw allows attackers to gain unauthorized control over host configurations, databases, and managed websites.

articles.title: Digital attacks drive a new wave of cargo theft, FBI says
articles.summary: The FBI has issued an alert regarding a significant rise in cyber-enabled cargo theft, as hackers increasingly target brokers and carriers to facilitate logistics-based crimes. This shift indicates that digital attack methods are rapidly replacing traditional cargo theft techniques.

articles.title: Cybercrime Groups Using Vishing and SSO Abuse in Rapid SaaS Extortion Attacks
articles.summary: Threat actors identified as Cordial Spider and Snarky Spider are executing rapid, high-impact SaaS extortion attacks using vishing and SSO exploitation. These campaigns are noted for their speed, high data-theft volume, and ability to operate with minimal forensic traces.

articles.title: Cyber incident responders who carried out ransomware attacks given 4-year sentences
articles.summary: Two cybersecurity incident responders were sentenced to four years in prison for abusing their professional access to conduct covert ransomware attacks. The case highlights the insider threat posed by individuals in trusted security roles.

articles.title: Criminal IP and Securonix ThreatQ Collaborate to Enhance Threat Intelligence Operations
articles.summary: Criminal IP and Securonix have partnered to integrate exposure-based threat intelligence into the ThreatQ platform to streamline and accelerate security incident investigations.

articles.title: China-Linked Hackers Target Asian Governments, NATO State, Journalists, and Activists
articles.summary: China-linked threat actor SHADOW-EARTH-053 is conducting a wide-reaching espionage campaign targeting government, defense, and civil society entities across Asia and a NATO member state. The operation, disclosed by Trend Micro, focuses on stealing sensitive information through sophisticated cyber activities.

articles.title: Criminal IP and Securonix ThreatQ Collaborate to Enhance Threat Intelligence Operations
articles.summary: Criminal IP and Securonix ThreatQ have formed a partnership to integrate their technologies to improve threat intelligence operations and cybersecurity monitoring. This collaboration aims to provide enhanced data and insights for security teams to detect and respond to threats more effectively.

articles.title: British cyber agency warns of looming ‘patch wave’ as AI speeds flaw discovery
articles.summary: The British cyber agency warns that AI-driven discovery of security vulnerabilities will necessitate a significant increase in urgent software patching. This trend poses a heightened risk of widespread exploitation across organizations.

articles.title: First reports come in of victims of critical cPanel vuln as 'millions' of sites potentially exposed
articles.summary: Reports indicate that a critical vulnerability in cPanel is now being actively exploited, potentially impacting millions of websites worldwide. Users are urged to patch their systems immediately to mitigate the risk of compromise.

articles.title: Carding service Jerry’s Store leak exposes 345,000 stolen payment cards
articles.summary: The carding service Jerry’s Store inadvertently exposed 345,000 stolen payment cards due to an insecurely configured server. This incident highlights a security lapse within a criminal platform used for testing stolen financial data.

articles.title: Download: Automating Pentest Delivery Guide
articles.summary: This guide provides strategies for modernizing penetration testing workflows by replacing manual, document-based processes with automated, continuous reporting systems. The goal is to enhance collaboration and speed up the delivery of actionable vulnerability findings.

articles.title: Cyber spies target Russian aviation firms to steal satellite and GPS data
articles.summary: A cyber-espionage group is targeting Russian aviation companies and government agencies to illicitly obtain sensitive satellite and GPS data. This campaign highlights a targeted effort to compromise critical geospatial information within the Russian defense and aviation sectors.

articles.title: Microsoft fixes Remote Desktop warnings displaying incorrectly
articles.summary: Microsoft has resolved a bug that caused Windows security warnings to display incorrectly when launching Remote Desktop (.rdp) files. This fix ensures that security prompts are correctly presented to users when initiating remote connections.

articles.title: OpenAI locks GPT-5.5-Cyber behind velvet rope despite slamming Anthropic for doing exactly that
articles.summary: OpenAI is facing criticism for restricting access to its latest model, GPT-5.5-Cyber, despite having previously criticized Anthropic for implementing similar access limitations. This highlights ongoing industry debates regarding the transparency and accessibility of advanced AI security models.

articles.title: Microsoft now lets admins choose pre-installed Store apps to uninstall
articles.summary: Microsoft has expanded its Windows 11 policy to allow IT administrators to select and uninstall specific pre-installed Microsoft Store apps from managed devices. This update provides greater control over system bloat and attack surface reduction within enterprise environments.

articles.title: Pro-Iran crew turns DDoS into shakedown as Ubuntu.com stays down
articles.summary: A pro-Iran threat group is utilizing DDoS attacks to extort organizations, resulting in a prolonged outage for the Ubuntu.com website. This shift marks a transition from purely disruptive attacks to financially motivated shakedowns.

articles.title: Critical cPanel Vulnerability Lets Attackers Bypass Login, Gain Root Access
articles.summary: A critical vulnerability in cPanel allows unauthorized users to bypass authentication and achieve root-level access, with evidence of active exploitation in the wild.

articles.title: Top Five Sales Challenges Costing MSPs Cybersecurity Revenue
articles.summary: Managed Service Providers are failing to capture significant cybersecurity market growth due to a misalignment between technical service offerings and business-centric sales strategies. This disconnect results in lost revenue opportunities despite the projected expansion of the managed security services sector.

articles.title: Two Cybersecurity Professionals Get 4-Year Sentences in BlackCat Ransomware Attacks
articles.summary: Two former cybersecurity professionals have been sentenced to four years in prison each for deploying BlackCat ransomware against multiple U.S. victims throughout 2023. The sentencing follows a Department of Justice investigation into their roles in facilitating these cyberattacks.

articles.title: Poisoned Ruby Gems and Go Modules Exploit CI Pipelines for Credential Theft
articles.summary: Attackers are distributing malicious Ruby gems and Go modules through a GitHub account to compromise CI/CD pipelines, enabling credential theft and persistent unauthorized access. This supply chain campaign leverages sleeper packages to maintain a low profile while delivering secondary malicious payloads.

articles.title: Passport to £££: Home Office adds £216M to travel doc contract before a single bid's been placed
articles.summary: The UK Home Office has increased the value of a pending travel document contract by £216 million before initiating the formal bidding process. This decision raises concerns regarding procurement transparency and potential financial mismanagement within government infrastructure projects.

articles.title: Anthropic launches Claude Security to counter rapid AI-Powered exploits
articles.summary: Anthropic has introduced Claude Security, a defensive tool designed to help organizations detect and mitigate the rapid increase in AI-driven cyberattacks. This launch comes in response to emerging malicious models like Mythos that enable near-instant exploitation of vulnerabilities.

articles.title: SonicWall patches three SonicOS flaws in Gen 6, 7 and 8 firewalls. Patch them now
articles.summary: SonicWall has released urgent firmware updates to address three vulnerabilities across Gen 6, 7, and 8 firewalls that could lead to unauthorized access and security control bypass. Administrators are advised to apply these patches immediately.

articles.title: Best Diagram Software in 2026, Why EdrawMax Works for Everyday Use
articles.summary: The article evaluates top diagramming software for 2026, highlighting Wondershare EdrawMax for its AI-powered features and template library.

articles.title: Open-source privacy proxy masks PII before prompts reach external AI services
articles.summary: Dataiku has released Kiji Privacy Proxy, an open-source tool designed to detect and mask personally identifiable information (PII) in prompts before they are sent to external AI APIs. This solution helps enterprise developers prevent accidental data leakage when interacting with third-party large language models.

articles.title: Shadow AI risks deepen as 31% of users get no employer training
articles.summary: A global survey reveals that up to one-third of employees use AI tools without employer oversight or training, creating significant security gaps. This trend of 'Shadow AI' highlights a growing misalignment between rapid workforce adoption and corporate governance controls.

articles.title: Identity is the control plane for distributed infrastructure
articles.summary: Teleport CEO Ev Kontsevoy advocates for consolidating fragmented identity systems into a single identity layer to improve security and visibility across distributed infrastructure. This approach emphasizes reducing credentials and entry points to better manage modern cloud and Kubernetes environments.
